title: Steering Column Multifunction Switch LH
introduction: This repair removes and refits the left-hand multifunction switch after opening the steering column shrouds. The column carries your steering input; the switch mounted beside it has a separate electrical job. I treat the plastic covers like a clamshell: find and release their catches before asking them to open. The linked access instructions below explain those movements. This is a replacement guide, not a test proving the switch caused a fault.

items.name: Shroud access tools
items.detail: Have an interior trim remover for the upper gap hider and a flat-bladed screwdriver for the shroud tabs.

items.name: Retainer tightening
items.detail: Use a torque tool capable of accurately applying the small installation torque given beside switch removal.

items.name: Prevent an unexpected start
items.detail: Park on level ground with the parking brake applied and wheels chocked; keep P selected on an automatic or a parked gear on a manual. Disable remote start, if equipped, through Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup before dismantling anything. Otherwise, someone could remotely start the car, causing personal injury or death. If the setting needs ignition power, select engine-off ON only from confirmed OFF by pressing START/STOP without pressing either pedal; after the setting change, return ON to OFF without pressing a pedal. Keep the engine stopped throughout. Retain the valid intelligent access key inside only for the mechanical column positioning and wheel rotations described below; remove it before disturbing the switch or its terminals. An accidental start during service can cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Personal protection
items.detail: Wear eye and ear protection while servicing the vehicle. Wear protective gloves when handling pointed or sharp-edged parts. Ignoring these precautions may cause serious personal injury. See [Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693189).

edits.text: NOTE: The illustrations show LHD (left-hand drive); RHD (right-hand drive) is similar.
edits.why: Use the illustrated arrangement to understand the attachments while allowing for the different driving position.

edits.text: NOTE: The removal steps also contain installation details; keep those details available for refitting.
edits.why: The torque beside switch removal is a tightening specification for installation.

edits.text:
Remove the upper and lower steering column shrouds.
Refer to: [Steering Column Shrouds](#/document/G1692617) (501-05 Interior Trim and Ornamentation, Removal and Installation).
edits.why: With ignition OFF, keep the valid intelligent access key inside for mechanical shroud access: entering with it unlocks an equipped steering-wheel lock. If the wheel cannot rotate, do not force it or switch ignition ON around exposed parts; stop for the matching steering-lock instructions. Lower the adjustment lever beneath the column to release the adjustment mechanism, then fully extend and lower the column and secure the adjustment lever again. At the gap hider between the instrument cluster and upper shroud, use an interior trim remover to release the attachment tabs and lift the gap hider upward off its attachment to the upper shroud; position it aside. Viewed from the driver's seat, rotate the steering wheel 90 degrees counterclockwise and release the exposed shroud tab with a flat-bladed screwdriver. Then rotate the wheel 180 degrees clockwise and release the opposite tab with the screwdriver. Release the outer clips along both sides of the upper shroud and lift the upper shroud away. Remove the lower-shroud screws from underneath, including the recessed attachment shown in the linked reference, and remove the lower shroud. This exposes the switch mounting without treating the covers as something to pry apart by force. With shroud access complete, confirm ignition OFF and remove the key from the vehicle before touching the switch or its terminals.

edits.text: NOTICE: Keep the component terminals straight and undamaged during removal and installation.
edits.why: The switch's electrical connection depends on intact terminals. I keep their alignment in view as the switch comes free and goes back into place.

edits.text: NOTE: The steering wheel is omitted from the illustration for clarity.
edits.why: That clearer view is not an instruction to remove the steering wheel; the shroud access sequence uses the installed wheel to expose the tabs.

edits.text:
Remove the retainers, then remove the LH steering column multifunction switch.
Installation torque: 9 lb.in (1 Nm)
edits.why: The illustration marks the retainers in magenta at the upper and lower mounting ears of the blue switch body. Release those attachments before removing the switch, while protecting its terminals. The stated torque belongs to these retainers when the switch is refitted.

edits.text: Install in reverse removal order: refit the switch without bending or damaging its terminals, install and tighten its retainers to the specified torque, then refit the steering column shrouds.
edits.why:
Refit the lower shroud and its screws before the upper shroud. Only after switch seating, terminal connection and fastening are complete, bring the valid key inside for the necessary mechanical wheel rotations, keeping ignition OFF. Engage the upper shroud's outer clips and released tabs, then reconnect the upper gap hider to the upper shroud. Reverse the access movements to restore the steering wheel position. Release the column-adjustment lever, restore the column position, then raise the lever to lock the column securely. Confirm the released cover attachments are engaged.

After all reassembly, remove tools and keep the car parked, chocked and restrained by its parking brake. With the valid key inside, press and release START/STOP from confirmed OFF without pressing either pedal to select ON with the engine stopped. Operate the LH lever up and down and check the corresponding exterior direction indicators and dashboard indications, returning the lever to center between checks. Set the separate lighting dial to the headlamp symbol; push the LH lever forward for high beam, then forward again or toward you to return to low beam. Pull the lever slightly toward you and release it to check the headlamp flasher. Keep observers out of the headlamp beams. These are ordinary completion checks, not fault isolation. Whether they pass or fail, center the indicators, turn the lighting control and high beams OFF, return ignition ON to OFF without pressing a pedal and remove the key. Keep ignition OFF and the key outside before any renewed switch inspection; an abnormal result needs the matching lighting diagnosis.
